As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for an outright ban on students using phones on campus.

With the new school year officially underway, the chorus of voices supporting classroom iPhone bans continues to grow.

Yes, although it's still July, summer has come to an end without us noticing. Over the next two days, my kids will head back to school — this is the second year in a row that the start of the school year falls outside August.

Apple is running its annual "Back to School" promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card of up to US$150. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday deals.

While back-to-school discounts are certainly a welcome perk, the growing trend of smartphone use in classrooms is increasingly meeting with pushback.

The most-liked comment was posted by Steve.

I have not seen any data to support the claim that 'allowing students to use phones during school shootings reduces risk.' In reality, the only way to truly uphold the mission of education is to reduce distractions in the classroom.

A recent Pew Research Center survey shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class — up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025 — with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for an all-day phone ban from class to dismissal is growing even faster. The share of Americans backing an all-day ban has, for the first time, overtaken those opposed.

The report also notes that while support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger people remain less supportive of both classroom and all-day bans. The full report is available here.

What's your take? Should schools restrict iPhones to classroom use only, implement an all-day ban from class to dismissal, or leave the decision to students and parents? Share your thoughts in the comments.
